subject: Control-plane bridge interface and evidence pack for Dedicated/Private
messages:
From: Ellie Thompson <ellie.t@acme.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: control-plane bridge/interface detail + CAIQ items

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. Acme's security team would like a short deliverable we can add to our risk file: a concise network diagram showing how Redwood's control plane and tenant-bridging behave for Dedicated and Private deployments, plus a short narrative describing isolation guarantees, egress touchpoints, and what customer-managed VPNs see.

Specific asks:
- One-page diagram (PDF/PNG) annotated with data/control plane boundaries.
- Callouts for what we consider "bridged" vs "fenced" traffic.
- CAIQ/SIG snapshot or the relevant responses for the network/security section (just the answers and evidence references).
- A short evidence index (what file proves what).

We need this by COB Thursday (2026-10-15) to include in our internal review. If anything is sensitive, mark it and we can treat it as confidential under our NDA.

Best,
Ellie Thompson
Security Programs Lead
Acme Corporation
ellie.t@acme.com

---
Attachment: (none in initial request)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Thompson <ellie.t@acme.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: control-plane bridge/interface detail + CAIQ items

Hi Ellie — thanks, we can do that. I attached a one-page starting point and looped in our security + infra leads to finalize evidence references.

What I'm sending now:
- redwood_controlplane_splitter_onepager.pdf (high-level diagram + bullets)

Short summary:
- Control plane (Redwood-managed): handles routing, model selection, and orchestration. Runs in a logically separated network and is not on the customer VLAN in Private deployments.
- Data/Inference plane (customer workload): runs in Dedicated pools or private VPCs; tenant traffic is fenced.
- Bridge/managed VPN: when customers choose a bridged VPN for low-latency, only the inference egress path is routed; control-plane signals remain on the Redwood-managed control channel.

Action items (internal): Kim — can you add the SIG/CAIQ snapshot and an evidence index we can share? Marcus — please produce an annotated bridge sketch showing the egress touchpoint for customer VPNs (brief SVG/png).

If anything sensitive is required, we'll mark the files accordingly. I'll follow up when we've consolidated the CAIQ responses.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood_controlplane_splitter_onepager.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-13T08:32:00-07:00

Stephanie / Marcus — quick internal notes and proposed redlines before we send to Acme: 

> On 2026-10-12T11:05:00-07:00, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai wrote:
> > Control plane (Redwood-managed): handles routing, model selection, and orchestration. Runs in a logically separated network and is not on the customer VLAN in Private deployments.

Two things to call out explicitly in the final narrative:
1) Control-plane authenticity: we sign control-plane RPCs and provide an audit trail for model rollouts (include retention window reference). Evidence: controlplane-audit-sample.log (we'll link in the drive).
2) Egress observability: when a customer opts for bridged VPN, only inference outbound flows traverse the customer tunnel; metadata and control updates continue over our control plane (no customer access to KV caches). Evidence: packetflow-sample.pcap (redacted) + network-bridge-annotated.png.

Marcus — can you generate the annotated-bridge-sketch.svg with the following callouts: NAT/egress gateway, TLS termination points, and optional HSM/KMS boundary if the customer uses a private KMS? Keep it technical but single-page.

I'll prepare the CAIQ network answers (A.1.* and A.2.*) and put them in a zip with references. Mark anything with customer-sensitive info as "CONFIDENTIAL - PRC" so Ellie knows to treat it accordingly.

Attachment: annotated-bridge-sketch.svg (SVG, 48KB)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Principal Security Architect | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: security@acme.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-14T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: control-plane bridge/interface detail + CAIQ items

Hi Ellie — attached is our consolidated packet for Acme. Summary and next steps are below.

Attachments included:
- redwood_controlplane_splitter_final.pdf — final annotated diagram + short narrative (PDF)
- network-bridge-annotated.png — high-res diagram export (PNG)
- caiaq-sig-pack-redwood.zip — CAIQ answers (network/security sections) and supporting evidence references
- evidence-index.csv — CSV mapping CAIQ control IDs to file names and short descriptions

Key points (10-line summary):
- Our control plane is logically separated from customer inference workloads; control RPCs are authenticated and logged.
- Dedicated pools run on isolated tenant scheduling; private installs can be air-gapped per contract.
- Bridged VPNs only carry inference egress; we do not expose control-plane KV caches or orchestration channels to customer networks.
- Egress gateways include TLS termination; optional private KMS integrations keep keys within the customer's KMS if configured.
- We've marked two files as sensitive (packetflow-sample.pcap, controlplane-audit-sample.log) — those are in the zip with the CONFIDENTIAL tag.

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical sync with Marcus and Kimberly to walk the diagrams and answer any follow-ups. Would Thursday 10/15 at 10:00am PT work for your team?

If you need any redactions before we send to a wider reviewer group, tell us which items to redact and we'll produce a redacted digest.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
